name: oxo-flow-rnaseq-star-deseq2
title: RNA-seq: STAR alignment, DESeq2 differential expression and QC
excluded: bwa_index — no consumer in the upstream default path
genome_faidx — no consumer in the upstream default path
edger — not present in upstream v3.1.1
kallisto — not present in upstream v3.1.1
trimgalore — not present in upstream v3.1.1 (fastp is the trimmer)
trimming.activate=false rewiring (star_align from raw reads) — default path only
SRA units sharing one accession — each SRA unit downloads its own reads (explicit-config simplification)
Snakemake report artifacts (report/*.rst) — no oxo-flow equivalent
per-unit fastp_adapters/fastp_extra lookup — pipeline-level config instead
description: End-to-end RNA-seq differential-expression analysis with STAR and DESeq2: Ensembl reference download, fastp trimming (paired-end and single-end), SRA read download (fasterq-dump, DRAFT), STAR alignment with gene counts, RSeQC QC + MultiQC, count matrix with technical-replicate collapse, Ensembl biomaRt gene-symbol annotation, and DESeq2 (normalized counts, PCA plots, per-contrast results with ashr shrinkage and MA plots, complex string-form contrasts via R expressions). Every tool is pinned to an exact conda version for reproducibility.

requirements: FASTQ reads per config/units.tsv (raw/<unit-key>_R1.fastq.gz / _R2.fastq.gz) and sample conditions in config/samples.tsv — paired-end by default; single-end and SRA modes are DRAFT (se_units / sra_units sample groups, both empty by default)
reference genome + annotation downloaded automatically from Ensembl release 115 (GRCh38) — network access required (also for biomaRt gene-symbol annotation)
compute: up to 24 CPUs per rule (star_align); 8 (fastp_pe); 4 (star_index/fastp_se); no per-rule memory limits configured in the workflow
disk: several tens of GB — ~30 GB GRCh38 STAR index, plus BAMs and trimmed reads
